goal: Make incomplete generated-project setup deterministic and gate releases on one configured project-validation command.

tasks.name: Add failing readiness fixtures
inputs: REQ-001 and its US-1 acceptance criteria
Approved PRD and README contracts from design.md
tasks.description: Create table-driven temporary-repository fixtures before implementing the checker. Cover markers and known boilerplate, exact ordered PRD headings, requirement subsections and references, README structure, hook configuration, simultaneous failures, stable diagnostic identifiers, affected paths, actionable remediation, and readiness exit statuses. Use a hostile hook canary and before/after fixture snapshot to detect execution or mutation by readiness inspection.

tests: Untouched, marker-only-deletion, and known-boilerplate fixtures fail
Heading order, duplication, case, and additional-section fixtures behave as specified
Requirement declaration, reference, malformed ID, duplicate ID, missing body, and fenced-example fixtures behave as specified
README title, Setup, Validation, and canonical-command fixtures behave as specified
Missing, non-executable, sentinel-bearing, and configured hook fixtures behave as specified
Multiple independent failures are reported together and internal errors are separate
A hostile hook canary is not triggered and fixture content and executable modes are unchanged
acceptance: Tests initially fail because scripts/check-project-readiness.py does not exist
Every document and hook acceptance criterion has positive and negative coverage
Tests assert diagnostic identifiers, affected paths, remediation presence, and statuses without freezing complete prose
Canary and snapshot assertions prove the checker does not execute scripts/validate-project.py or mutate the fixture

tasks.name: Implement readiness inspection and initial hook
inputs: REQ-001, REQ-006, and their mapped design criteria
Python 3.11+ and the standard library available on the supported GitHub-hosted Linux runner
Readiness status contract: 0 ready, 1 unready, 2 usage or internal error
tasks.description: Implement read-only, no-argument Python readiness inspection from the repository root. Parse headings outside fenced code blocks, report all independent failures with stable identifiers, affected paths, and next actions, and distinguish observable unready state from internal errors. Add the executable adopter-owned Python hook with its exact sentinel, setup guidance, and status 1. Implement the Python template contract validator and require all public Python scripts without invoking the hook.

tests: scripts/test-project-readiness.py
scripts/test-portable-validation.sh
Python compilation and tests
acceptance: Readiness inspection never mutates files or executes the project hook
All independent readiness failures are emitted before status 1
Usage and evaluation failures emit INTERNAL_READINESS_ERROR and status 2
The initial hook is executable, includes the exact sentinel, prints setup guidance, and exits 1
No Ripgrep or Nix dependency is introduced

tasks.name: Add canonical repository validation
inputs: REQ-002 and its US-2 acceptance criteria
Readiness checker and status contract from T2
tasks.description: Test and implement the no-argument generated-project Python validation command. Run template validation, readiness inspection, and project validation in order; print stable stage labels; stop before later stages after failure; and preserve the exact first failing status.

tests: Each stage can fail independently
A minimally configured repository passes all stages
Arbitrary non-zero project-hook statuses propagate exactly
Later stages do not run after an earlier failure
acceptance: Stage order and labels are stable and observable
Template validation and readiness inspection are read-only; adopter-hook toolchain and artifact effects remain adopter-owned
Readiness inspection tests remain separate from hook execution tests
Python compilation and tests pass

tasks.name: Test and wire active CI and release topology
inputs: REQ-003, REQ-006, and their mapped design criteria
Existing CI workflow and delivery-contract tests
tasks.description: Add tests scoped to active YAML job structure and wire the exact project-validation job with display name Project validation. Source mode runs readiness and aggregate fixtures only when github.repository matches the explicit workflow constant; generated mode runs python3 scripts/validate-repository.py. Run on ubuntu-latest for the ordinary pull_request, push, and manual workflow events; prohibit pull_request_target execution of contributor code, attached environments, checkout ref overrides from privileged events, failure-tolerant validation, secrets, write permissions, and persisted checkout credentials. Add project-validation to the release dependency list and reject release conditions that can run after its failure.

tests: Commented matches and unrelated jobs cannot satisfy the workflow contract
Missing generated-mode invocation or incorrect source comparison fails
Elevated permissions, persisted credentials, or secret references fail
Unsupported runner or event trust, attached environment, and unsafe checkout ref overrides fail
continue-on-error on the validation job or canonical command step fails
A release job without project-validation in active needs or with a failure-bypassing condition fails
Source and generated branches invoke their intended commands
Every pull request emits the stable Project validation check name
acceptance: scripts/test-delivery-contract.py passes for the real workflow
Actionlint passes
Existing source release dependencies remain intact
The validation job receives no secrets or write-capable permissions
The adopter hook runs only inside the approved GitHub-hosted event and runner boundary

tasks.name: Add GitHub snapshot conformance
inputs: REQ-004, REQ-005, and their mapped design criteria
tasks.description: Build a deterministic release-tree manifest from paths already tracked by Git plus the plan's explicit new generated-project scripts, then copy their current working-tree content and executable modes into a temporary repository without Copier exclusions. Exclude Git metadata, ignored files, and unrelated untracked files; assert all required validation scripts are present. Prove the untouched snapshot fails, minimally configure PRD, README, and the hook, then prove aggregate validation passes. Add this and the source-maintainer fixture suites to source CI and Nix checks.

tests: Direct-copy untouched snapshot emits expected readiness identifiers
Direct-copy minimally configured snapshot passes aggregate validation
Maintenance artifacts retained by GitHub do not change readiness
Ignored and unrelated untracked canaries are excluded while required new scripts and executable modes are preserved
Source CI and Nix checks execute readiness, aggregate, and GitHub snapshot suites
acceptance: The fixture applies no Copier behavior
Both failure and success paths pass locally
nix flake check includes the new source-maintainer evidence

tasks.name: Strengthen Copier copy and update coverage
inputs: REQ-004, REQ-005, and their mapped design criteria
tasks.description: Prove an untouched Copier-generated project fails and a minimally configured project passes. Configure Copier to skip an existing adopter-owned hook during updates, customize that hook, and change the same hook in the newer template version. Accept preservation only when the update succeeds, adopter content remains, and non-conflicting upstream content appears. Accept conflict only when Copier's pinned status or diagnostic and explicit conflict evidence are present and adopter content remains recoverable. Fail closed on any other error or content loss. Exclude only declared Copier-specific maintenance fixtures and keep update claims scoped to Copier-generated projects.

tests: Untouched Copier output fails with expected readiness identifiers
Minimally configured Copier output passes aggregate validation
Preservation requires success, retained adopter content, and applied non-conflicting upstream content
Conflict requires pinned Copier conflict status or diagnostic, explicit conflict evidence, and recoverable adopter content
Unrelated Copier failures are not accepted as conflicts
A silent-overwrite simulation fails
Declared maintenance-only fixtures are absent from Copier output
acceptance: scripts/test-copier.py passes with Copier 9.17.0
The test records and asserts the observed pinned update behavior
No custom update or file-ownership mechanism is introduced
GitHub snapshot packaging is not constrained by Copier exclusions

tasks.name: Align project-facing documentation
inputs: REQ-001 through REQ-006 and their mapped design criteria
GitHub snapshot and Copier update distinction
tasks.description: Add the README marker and align documentation on the canonical generated-project command, source fixture commands, PRD and README structure, adopter-owned hook, diagnostics, guarantee limits, manual ruleset setup using the exact Project validation check name, and semantic-major compatibility rule. Qualify every Copier prerequisite and update claim so GitHub snapshots remain an independent one-time generation path. Extend the delivery-contract test to own semantic documentation assertions. Keep deferred follow-ups outside current onboarding promises.

tests: Markdownlint for changed Markdown
scripts/test-delivery-contract.py documentation path, command, and stable check-name assertions
Search for stale quality, update-lineage, merge-gate, and source-mode claims
acceptance: Generated documentation names python3 scripts/validate-repository.py consistently
Source documentation names fixture commands instead of a hidden bypass
The six onboarding actions include manual merge-gate configuration
Ruleset guidance names the exact Project validation check emitted for every pull request
GitHub snapshots are described as one-time and Copier projects as update-capable
No deferred follow-up appears as current implementation behavior

tasks.name: Verify the complete readiness contract
inputs: REQ-001 through REQ-006 and their mapped design criteria
tasks.description: Run repository-defined validation and inspect the full diff for scope, ownership, security, compatibility, and generated-state violations. Confirm source CI behavior and both generated-project paths have local evidence. Run substantive code review and address approved findings through the normal review workflow.

tests: scripts/validate-template.py
scripts/test-project-readiness.py
scripts/test-repository-validation.py
scripts/test-github-template-readiness.py
scripts/test-copier.py
Python compilation and tests
Actionlint for all workflows
nix flake check
Markdownlint for changed Markdown
git diff --check
Targeted stale-contract searches
acceptance: All repository-defined validation passes with fresh output
The final diff contains no secrets, local settings, generated agent state, or unrelated changes
Source mode and both generation paths have failure and success evidence
verification-before-completion evidence is reported before any completion claim
